The main takeaway from our work is that

the presence of a ridge subducting beneath a continental margin can have a profound effect on the dynamics of the overriding lithosphere, and that these effects can be captured in 3-D laboratory experiments.

the dynamics of subduction is sensitive to the presence of a subducting ridge and that these sensitivities are strongly controlled by the orientation of the ridge relative to the trench and the subducting plate.

subducting ridged lithosphere can cause significant perturbations to the mantle wedge flow, including the formation of secondary convection cells, the formation of a double diffusive layer, and changes to the mantle flow direction.
